messages:
Alex (Customer): hi team — we deprovisioned several users via SCIM this morning but they still have product access. I removed them from the IdP group and our provisioning logs show 200, but they can still call the API.
Anna (CS): sorry to hear that — can you paste the SCIM payload and the provisioning audit id?
Alex (Customer): payload id: p-9f3b. here's the /Groups PATCH we sent: ```{
  \"schemas\": [\"urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp\"],
  \"Operations\": [{
    \"op\": \"remove\",
    \"path\": \"members[value eq \"user:alice@example.com\"]\"
  }]
}``` we also got HTTP/1.1 200 OK from your endpoint.
Anna (CS): thanks — that matches what we see in our webhook delivery logs: 200 returned by our SCIM worker. Which role mapping should have been removed?
Alex (Customer): group -> role mapping is: externalId = team-ops, role = ops:admin. The user was removed from group in Okta at 09:12 UTC. Deprovision event shows in our IdP logs and in your delivery at 09:13.
Jules (Support): quick question — is the API key usage tied to a token that was minted earlier and cached? We have a cache for role grants that can be up to 15m, but not hours.
Mike (IAM): pinging this thread. Looking at the tenant state: user alice@example.com still has role ops:admin attached in RBAC store. SCIM worker accepted the patch but downstream binder that attaches roles to tokens returned 404 for the role lookup at 09:13 and retried; it eventually marked as success but didn't remove the cached grant.
Mike (IAM): possible root causes: 1) group externalId mismatch (case or prefix) — the SCIM patch removed member from group 'team-ops' but our mapping is on 'org:team-ops'. 2) deprovision path for users vs group-removal behaves differently — group removal sends Member removal events while full user deprovision sends removeUser. 3) RBAC cache TTL (we have a 1h rolling cache for grants for performance)
Alex (Customer): we definitely use plain team-ops; no  org: prefix. Our group externalId in Okta shows team-ops.
Anna (CS): can you run a manual lookup to confirm server-side group membership? Try: ```curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED\" \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/tenants/tenant-abc/groups?externalId=team-ops\"``` and also check user grants: ```curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED\" \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/tenants/tenant-abc/users?email=alice@example.com\"```
Alex (Customer): ran both — group shows empty members, user shows ops:admin still present in grants array.
Mike (IAM): OK that nails it: SCIM worker removed group member, but the grant detachment job is queued asynchronously and failed to purge for alice due to a transient DB deadlock at 09:14 (we have logs). The worker retried and marked as delivered but grant cleanup errored.
SCIM Bot: EVENT: delivery_id=p-9f3b status=200 response_time_ms=512 ack=SCIM_WORKER_03
Mike (IAM): next steps: 1) I'll kick the manual grant reconciliation for tenant-abc (one-time job) and force-expire caches for alice. 2) We'll add a safety reconcile that triggers if group->role mapping removal succeeds but user still has role after 2 reconciliation windows.
Anna (CS): Alex, sorry for the break. We should have this cleaned up in ~15 minutes after the reconciliation finishes. I'll follow up here when done and include logs.
Alex (Customer): thanks. Can you also confirm whether token scope/refresh will require user logout to lose access?
Mike (IAM): short answer: tokens already minted that include the role claim will remain valid until they expire (we issue short-lived access tokens, default 1h). However refresh/renewed tokens will get updated claims immediately after reconciliation. If you need immediate revocation we can revoke all active sessions for the user — tell us and we'll do it.
Jules (Support): documenting repro: 1) IdP removes user from group -> 2) SCIM PATCH delivered (200) -> 3) group->role mapping triggers async grant cleanup job -> 4) transient DB error prevents grant removal -> 5) cached grant remains until reconcile/TTL.
Anna (CS): follow-up action items assigned: Mike to run manual reconcile and post job id; Engineering to add alert for reconcile mismatches; Support to notify customer of revocation options.
Mike (IAM): manual reconcile started job id rc-202324: queued 09:22, processing 09:23. Kicking cache for alice now.
SCIM Bot: RECONCILE rc-202324 status=success removed_grants=1 affected_users=[alice@example.com]
Anna (CS): confirmed alice no longer has ops:admin in grants. Alex, can you re-test API call that previously worked?
Alex (Customer): re-tested — returns 403 now. Good. Thanks for quick turnaround.
Anna (CS): closing the incident but we'll keep the alert and follow-up engineering ticket open: ENG-1234. :thumbsup:
